name: 12 Step
summary: Covers original 12 Step hardware, the dedicated bootloader added in firmware 1.0.0, and the newer 12 Step2 hardware with named ports.

notes: Applies the same two firmware-update settings its sibling KMI families need (see softstep.json / boppad.json / qunexus.json), for the MODERN chunked --fw-update path to a 12 Step that already has a bootloader - NOT the legacy pre-1.0.0 trojan-bootloader install.

firstGapDelayMs (5000): the bootloader erases its whole application region when it recognizes the first firmware packet, blocking USB until that finishes - so chunk 1's reply can't come within the 100ms steady-state -cd. Without this, the first send attempt times out on chunk 1 and only the retry (after the erase is already done) succeeds. 5000ms lets the FIRST attempt wait it out. It's a return-early timeout (spent only if the reply is genuinely slow), so the generous value has no steady-state cost; confirm the real erase duration with --timestamp and tighten if desired.

rebootsToAppOnFinalChunk (true): 12 Step reboots straight into application mode as it commits the final chunk, so it never answers an identity request on the bootloader port afterwards. Skip the doomed final-chunk handshake and let runAutomaticUpdate's application-port reconnect + version check be the success test.
chunkDelayMs/postDelayMs left at CLI defaults (100/500). Validated on real hardware 2026-08-26 (12 Step v1.0.9): single-pass update, zero 'NO REPLY'/retries, app-port version confirmed.
Requests a reboot from the running application into bootloader mode.
Helps legacy units gain access to the dedicated bootloader flow.
Single unchunked payload, superseded by firmware_1_0_8's chunk-safe packaging.
Chunk-safe (-cs512) packaging via the shared Hex_to_SysEx tool, built from 12-step-firmware's SysEx_and_Hex_Images/make_sysex_app.ps1.
Addressed with product ID 21 (0x15, the bootloader's own PID) rather than either application hardware revision's PID (20/22), so it works unmodified for both 12step1 and 12step2.
Superseded by firmware_1_0_9's boot-tare capture and revised on/off threshold defaults.
Chunk-safe (-cs512) packaging via the shared Hex_to_SysEx tool, built from 12-step-firmware's SysEx_and_Hex_Images/make_sysex_app.ps1.
Addressed with product ID 21 (0x15, the bootloader's own PID) rather than either application hardware revision's PID (20/22), so it works unmodified for both 12step1 and 12step2.

Adds a 1-second boot-time tare capture for key/select sensors (margined +25%, clamped to 2/3 of the usable range) to reduce stuck-key false triggers, and raises the default on/off pressure thresholds (20/15) with an enforced off >= on/2 floor.
